text_simplified: Ibn al-Qayyim said that whoever neglects teaching his child what benefits him has done the utmost harm to him, and most corruption in children comes from parents neglecting them. Along with taking care of the foundations and means of tarbiyah, the parent must entrust his affair to Allah and rely upon Him in reforming his children, and not attach his heart to the means. Among that is the saying of Imam Malik: 'Good character is the character [taught] by Allah, not the character of fathers and mothers,' and in it is consolation for one who exerted his effort in reforming his child but it did not improve.

review_defects.why: The English drops the phrase 'نقل الشيخ' (the Shaykh conveyed), losing the attribution that this is a reported saying.
The Arabic frames it as 'The Shaykh conveyed the saying of Ibn al-Qayyim,' but the English drops 'نقل الشيخ' and presents it as a direct statement.
